mo_cm_columbia_area_bouldering.blurb: Bouldering and nothing else, spread around the south side of Columbia and out toward Ashland. The problems are grouped by creek: Three Creeks holds the most climbs, Middle River comes next, and Gans Creek and Cedar Creek follow. Development here is recent, though some of the boulders saw earlier, undocumented ascents. Grades run from V0 up into the V12 range, with the heaviest concentration around V4 and V5 and a thinner tail of hard problems. At Rooftown, one of the Three Creeks zones, the boulders sit close to the creek bed, which normally runs dry but can fill with feet of water after a heavy storm.

nc_cedar_rock.blurb: Cedar Rock is a mostly trad venue near Brevard, with a handful of sport routes and one ice line. The main cliff is granite, known for steep, intimidating face climbing, and it faces west, so it stays cool on summer mornings and picks up warmth on winter afternoons. The North side and the Main Wall hold the most climbs, with several multi-pitch lines on the Main Wall, and South Side is a big low-angle slab covered in grooves and faces. Grades mostly sit between 5.8 and 5.11, with fewer easy routes and only a few harder ones.

nc_whiteside_mountain.blurb: Whiteside Mountain sits between Highlands and Cashiers and is mostly a trad cliff, with a few sport routes and a winter ice scene on the north-facing sides. The grades are stiff: most rock routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12, and the ice runs from WI3 to WI5. Faces point in nearly every direction, so there is shade to be found in summer and sun in winter. The Southeast Face, about 700 feet tall, is the long multipitch wall, the North Face has routes of two to four pitches, and the Southwest Corner and the section left of the main face add shorter climbing. Long runouts between gear and loose rock are part of the reputation.

tn_dayton_pocket_laurel_falls_bouldering.blurb: Boulder problems near Dayton, north of Chattanooga, strung along a river and creek on sandstone. Vapor Lock Cave holds the most climbs, followed by the Trail Split Area, Riverdance Boulder and Hillside. The area is known for a large horizontal roof with sculpted pockets and pinches, whose rock stays dry in the rain, and there is also a boulder field on a south-facing hill. Grades lean hard: most problems sit between V7 and V11, with a smaller group of moderates below and a few at V12 and beyond. The surrounding Laurel Snow area is described as a good winter destination.

wi_east_bluff_07_railroad_tracks.blurb: Railroad Tracks is the stretch of East Bluff above the railroad line on the east shore of Devil's Lake, in the Baraboo Range. Climbing is mostly traditional, with a good number of top-rope lines and some boulders. Railroad Amphitheater holds the most climbs, followed by Horse Rampart, Birthday Rocks and Lothar's Ledges. Grades spread from beginner level to hard, with the most between 5.4 and 5.9. Across Devil's Lake the bluff rock is Baraboo quartzite, hard and glassy, so routes often feel harder than their grades, and the lake has no fixed bolts or anchors, so climbs are protected with removable gear.

al_buck_s_pocket.blurb: Buck's Pocket lies in the Sand Mountain region of north Alabama and is mostly a sport area, with some trad and a couple dozen boulder problems. It is still being developed. Sport grades run from 5.6 into the 5.12s, with the most routes between 5.9 and 5.12. Southwest Bucks and the Northeast Section hold the most climbs, the Southeast Section is centred on the Zero Gravity Wall, and Creekside holds most of the boulder problems.
